metadata.title: Soil advisory rule references
metadata.units: N, P and K in mg/kg (ppm); organic matter and moisture in percent
metadata.disclaimer: Reference bands are demonstration defaults. Confirm laboratory method, crop, season, soil type and local Soil Health Card guidance before applying fertilizer or amendment rates.

sources.name: Soil Health Card, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, India
sources.use: soil-test interpretation and field-specific nutrient planning

low.title: Nitrogen management
actions: Confirm the crop-specific nitrogen dose using the soil-test report and local Soil Health Card.
Split nitrogen applications to match crop demand and reduce avoidable losses.
Use composted manure, legumes or green manure where suitable.
low.caution: Do not apply a universal nitrogen rate; account for crop, soil, season and previous nutrient inputs.

high.title: Avoid extra nitrogen
actions: Review the full soil test and crop plan before adding nitrogen.
Avoid routine nitrogen application when the crop does not require it.
high.caution: A high test value is not, by itself, a diagnosis of toxicity.

low.title: Phosphorus management
actions: Confirm the crop-specific phosphorus dose from the Soil Health Card or local extension service.
Use locally recommended basal placement near the root zone.
Maintain organic matter and suitable crop residues.
low.caution: Phosphorus interpretation depends on the laboratory extraction method and local calibration.

high.title: Avoid extra phosphorus
actions: Review the soil-test method and crop plan before adding phosphorus.
Avoid routine phosphorus application until the recommendation is confirmed.
high.caution: A high test value is not, by itself, a diagnosis of toxicity.

low.title: Potassium management
actions: Confirm the crop-specific potassium dose from the Soil Health Card or local extension service.
Apply at the crop stage and placement advised locally.
Return suitable crop residues to the soil.
low.caution: Do not apply a universal potassium rate; follow locally calibrated soil-test advice.

high.title: Avoid extra potassium
actions: Review the soil-test method and crop plan before adding potassium.
Avoid routine potassium application until the recommendation is confirmed.
high.caution: A high test value is not, by itself, a diagnosis of toxicity.

acidic.title: Acid soil management
actions: Request lime-requirement or buffer-pH testing before selecting an application rate.
Use agricultural lime or dolomite only at a locally recommended rate.
Consider locally adapted acid-tolerant crops while soil constraints are addressed.
acidic.caution: Do not estimate a lime rate from pH alone; soil texture and buffer capacity matter.

alkaline.title: Alkaline soil assessment
actions: Check electrical conductivity, sodicity and irrigation-water quality before selecting an amendment.
Consult a local soil laboratory or extension service for a field-specific plan.
Maintain organic inputs where appropriate.
alkaline.caution: High pH alone does not establish sodicity or identify the correct amendment.

low.title: Build soil organic matter
actions: Use mature compost or well-decomposed manure where suitable.
Add green manure, cover crops or legumes when the rotation allows.
Avoid unnecessary residue burning.
low.caution: Account for nutrients in organic inputs and follow local nutrient-management guidance.

dry.title: Conserve soil moisture
actions: Use mulch and schedule irrigation according to crop stage, soil texture and weather.
dry.caution: A single moisture reading does not represent seasonal field water availability.

wet.title: Review excess wetness
actions: Check drainage, irrigation timing and compaction before adding fertilizer.
wet.caution: A single moisture reading does not represent seasonal field water availability.

balanced.title: Maintain balanced soil management
actions: Continue crop-specific soil-test planning and periodic testing.
balanced.caution: This prototype does not assess micronutrients, salinity, pests or disease.

soil_health_scoring.method: Arithmetic mean of six range-fit indicators: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, organic matter and moisture. Each indicator contributes equally; scores are bounded from 0 to 100.

crop_suitability.method: Weighted range-fit across crop requirements. Score is a compatibility indicator, not a guaranteed yield prediction.

rules.fertilizer: Use crop- and district-specific Soil Health Card guidance. Do not prescribe a universal kg/ha rate from these bands.
rules.fertilizer_application_guidance: Base fertilizer source, dose, timing and placement on the crop, soil-test method, season, local calibration and Soil Health Card. Split mobile nutrients when advised and avoid application immediately before heavy rain or irrigation.
rules.acid_soil: Request lime requirement or buffer-pH testing before selecting a lime or dolomite rate.
rules.alkaline_soil: Check EC, sodicity and irrigation-water quality before selecting an amendment.
